MINUTES
  ADJOURNED PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  AUGUST 20, 2018

An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called
to order at 6:15 p.m. in the Council Chamber at Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive
North, Rolling Hills Estates, California by CHAIR ROMANELLI.

2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  CHAIR ROMANELLI led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance

3.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  Chair Romanelli, Persichina, Retz, Wroan

  COMMISSIONERS ABSENT:  Pope, Portugal

  STAFF PRESENT:  Andy Clark, Community Services Director
  Heidi Luce, City Clerk
  Daniel A-Haja, Senior Recreation Leader

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES OF JULY 16, 2018

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA moved, seconded by VICE CHAIR RETZ,

  TO APPROVE THE MINUTES OF THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION
  MEETING OF JULY 16, 2018 AS PRESENTED.

  Hearing no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

A.  STREET TREE REMOVAL APPLICATION

  Community Services Director reviewed the street tree removal application on a property located
  at 27 Clubview Lane.

  VICE CHAIR RETZ moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER WROAN,

  TO APPROVE THE REMOVAL AND REPLACEMENT OF A BRAZILIAN PEPPER
  STREET TREE LOCATED AT 27 CLUBVIEW LANE AT THE COST OF THE
  APPLICANT.

  Hearing no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  “BUTCHER PARK” REVISED CONCEPTUAL DESIGN

  Community Services Director Clark reviewed the “Butcher Park” revised conceptual design from
  BMLA, including the proposed plant materials for the landscape planting.

  In response to COMMISSIONER WROAN’s inquiry regarding parking for the park, VICE CHAIR
  RETZ commented that the parking was discussed previously, noting that the park is designed to
  be more of a neighborhood park that residents could walk or bike to, but there is parking across
  the street adjacent to Dapplegray Park.

  VICE CHAIR RETZ commented that he would suggest, if possible, the use of plants that are
  native to the Palos Verdes Peninsula area like White Sage.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI called for comments from the public.

  Paul Moylan, resident of Hitching Post asked if the tree-house shown on the first page of the plan
  will be part of the plan because he did not see it noted the subsequent pages. Community
   Services Director Clark responded that it was the desire of the Commission to include some type
  of climbing structure and staff will ensure that such an apparatus is included in the final design.

  Sally Kinsey, resident of Pony Lane commented that the plants selected, although not necessarily
  native to the Palos Verdes Peninsula, are mostly very appropriate and will be low care and low
  maintenance. She further commented that the type of plants proposed on the plan would be more
  appropriate and create more of a park-like setting as opposed to Palos Verdes Peninsula native
  plants like those at the Nature Center. She further suggested the following alternatives to some
  of the plant proposed: Use Dessert Willow instead of Western Red Bud and Crepe Myrtle and
  use permeable paving instead of roses to allow for parking. She also suggested incorporating a
  circular path for tricycles to use.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI asked Ms. Kinsey to put her suggestions in writing and provide to staff for
  incorporation into the final plan where possible.

  VICE CHAIR RETZ expressed concern that the proposed slide may entice skateboards to use is
  as a ramp. He suggested that given its proximity to Palos Verdes Drive East, it may need to be
  redesigned.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA,

  TO APPROVE THE REVISED CONCEPTUAL DESIGN TO INCLUDE INCORPORATION
  OF THE COMMENTS MADE BY SALLY KINSEY AND VICE CHAIR RETZ RELATED TO
  THE PROPOSED PLANT MATERIALS AND SLIDE; AND MOVE FORWARD WITH
  PREPARATION OF THE BID PACKAGE AND PLANS FOR THE PROJECT.

  Hearing no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

B.  PARADE MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT

  Daniel A-Haja, Senior Recreation Leader presented the parade management agreement for the
  Commission’s consideration noting that this year’s agreement includes an increase of $250.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI expressed concern regarding the increase and questioned the reason for
  the increase. VICE CHAIR RETZ concurred with CHAIR ROMANELLI’S concern.

  COMMISSIONER WROAN also expressed concern, but suggested that maybe a deliverable, like
  the Certificate of Insurance, which is currently listed as an additional cost, could be included to
  justify the increase.

  Discussion ensued concerning the justification and rationale for the $250 increase in the contract
  costs. CHAIR ROMANELLI suggested that this matter be tabled until an accounting of costs is
  provided.

  Hearing no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI tabled consideration of this item. Staff was directed to
  confer with Pageantry Productions as to the justification and rationale for the increase and to
  provide an accounting of the costs associated with the contract.

C.  POCKET PARK PROJECT UPDATE

  Community Services Director Clark reviewed the preliminary concept plan and probable
  construction costs for the proposed pocket park located off Palos Verdes Drive East in the Harbor
  Sight neighborhood that is being funded by Harbor Sight residents, John and Lynne Taber. He
  noted that the proposed 5’ path would need to be revised to be at least 8’ in width so that
  maintenance and emergency vehicles can access it; and staff suggests that native trees, such as
  the California Sycamore, Catalina Island Cherry, or Coastal Live Oak be planted around the
  hitching post site instead of the proposed California Pepper trees, which are non-native trees.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI called for public comment.

  Andrea Vona, Palos Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy noted a drainage issue on private
  property that was recently discovered and suggested that the plan be revised to address the
  drainage outlet issue so that the proposed trail is not washed out in a rain event.

  VICE CHAIR RETZ expressed his sincere appreciation to the Tabers for their generosity in
  funding this project and commented that this park will be a wonderful addition to the City.

  Community Services Director Clark noted that the proposed name for the pocket park is “John &
  Lynn Taber Grove” and the official action to recommend a name the pocket park will be brought
  back before the Commission in September.

Park & Activities Commission Minutes  2
August 20, 2018
   COMMISSIONER WROAN moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA,

  TO APPROVE THE PRELIMINARY CONCEPT PLAN WITH INCORPORATION OF
  CHANGES TO ADDRESS THE ISSUES RAISED BY ANDREA VONA REGARDING THE
  DRAINAGE ISSUE AND BY STAFF REGARDING THE WIDTH OF THE PATHWAY AND
  THE PROPOSED TREES AND BRING THE MATTER BACK TO THE COMMISSION
  FOR FINAL APPROVAL AT THE SEPTEMBER MEETING.

  Hearing no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

D.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE ACTION ITEM

  Community Services Director Clark provided a brief summary and background on this matter
  stating that the Equestrian Committee recommends that the Park and Activities Commission
  make a recommendation to the City Council to expand the Chandler Park Horse Arena by 20 ft.
  at a cost of approximately $12,800

  Pam Schachter, resident of Ranchview Road expressed her opposition to the Equestrian
  Committee’s recommendation to expand Chandler Park Horse Arena. She commented that she
  does not believe it is a good use of funds nor would it be beneficial to the equestrian community
  in general. She also expressed safety concerns and that the equestrian community was not aware
  of the proposed change.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA commented that he concurs that it would not be a good use of
  funds.

  Discussion ensued concerning the funding available for the project and the impact increasing the
  size of the ring would have on the trees in the area.

  At COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA’S suggestion, Community Services Director Clark noted for
  the COMMISSION’S information that the judging booth at Ernie Howlett Park does not function
  as desired; and although a representative from the Portuguese Bend Horse Show had committed
  to funding correction of the deficiencies, they have since reneged on that offer and it will be up to
  the City to make the necessary modifications. He noted that this matter will be coming before the
  COMMISSION in the coming months.

  VICE CHAIR RETZ moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER WROAN,

  THAT THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ABANDON CONSIDERATION OF
  THE PROPOSED EXPANSION OF THE CHANDLER PARK ARENA.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

E.  TEMPORARY STREET BANNER METAL FRAME HOLDERS

  Community Services Director Clark provided a brief update to the previous discussion regarding
  the permanent plywood boards proposed for the temporary street banner locations. He
  commented that concern was expressed that they would be subject to graffiti and may not last
  very long, so it was proposed to create a metal frame holder with grommets instead. He noted
  that Mike Goldsmith will create a prototype to test the modified design; and if it works, they would
  be fabricated for all of the locations.

  Discussion ensued concerning use of the frames, the material to be used to fabricate them and
  cost. It was suggested that they be constructed in such manner so they do not rust and possibly
  be powder coated

  VICE CHAIR RETZ moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA,

  THAT THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION RECEIVE AND FILE THE REPORT
  ON THE TEMPORARY STREET BANNER METAL FRAM HOLDERS.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.
F.  CITY CELEBRATION PROMOTIONS

  Community Services Director Clark provided an update on the City Celebration promotions and
  shared the DRAFT promotional flyers and posters created by the Betty’s Foundation staff to
  promote both events, The City Celebration and the Remember the Music Fesitval.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA moved, seconded by VICE CHAIR RETZ,

Park & Activities Commission Minutes  3
August 20, 2018
   THAT THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION RECEIVE AND FILE THE REPORT
  ON THE CITY CELEBRATION PROMOTIONS.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

A.  ADOPT-A-PARK REPORTS

  VICE CHAIR RETZ noted that there are a few rails and one post that need to be repaired on
  Palos Verdes Drive East (near Clubwiew Lane)

B.  RACE SUBCOMMITTEE DEBRIEFING MEETING – SEPTEMBER 17, 2018 AT 5:00 P.M.

  Community Services Director Clark noted that there will be a Race Subcommittee debriefing
  meeting on September 17 at 5:00 p.m,

C.  PARADE SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING – SEPTEMBER 17, 2018 AT 6:00 P.M.

  Community Services Director Clark noted that there will be a Parade Subcommittee meeting on
  September 17 at 6:00 p.m.

  ***

  CHAIR ROMANELLI noted that he will not be in attendance at the September 17 meeting of the
  Park & Activities Commission and VICE CHAIR RETZ will chair that meeting.

9.  DIRECTOR’S ITEM

A.  CITY CELEBRATION BOOTH SHIFTS (sign-up sheet)

  Community Services Director circulated a sign-up sheet for City Celebration Booth Shifts.

B.  NATURE CENTER REPLACEMENT CENTER CONSULTANT SELECTION SUBCOMMITTEE

  Community Services Director Clark noted that a Request for Qualifications was send out to
  identify contractors that would be qualified to work on the RFQ and the COMMISSION should
  appoint a subcommittee to meet with staff to interview the firms for this project. VICE CHAIR
  RETZ expressed interest in serving on the subcommittee.

The above DIRECTOR’S ITEMS Items 9A and 9B were received and filed.

10.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF AUGUST 14, 2018

  CHAIR ROMANELLI commented that the City Council discussed and expressed concern
  regarding attendance. He noted that a letter will be sent to all Commissioners and Committee
  Members reminding them of the importance of attendance and participation

  At Community Service Director Clark’s request, City Clerk Luce briefly reviewed the
  Commission/Committee recruitment process noting that all Commissioners and Committee
  Members will be receiving a letter in early October asking if they are interested in being
  reappointed.

B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF JULY 10, 2018

C.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE DRAFT MINUTES OF JULY 30, 2018

The above MATTERS OF INFORMATION Items 10A, 10B and 10C were received and filed.

11.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

A.  COMMISSIONER ROLES DURING CITYWIDE DISASTERS – SEPTEMBER 17, 2018

  Community Services Director Clark stated that Alexa Davis, Assistant to the City Manager and
  Jessica Slawson, Administrative Analyst will attend the September 17 meeting to provide
  information on Commissioner’s roles during citywide disasters.

Park & Activities Commission Minutes  4
August 20, 2018
   ***

  CHAIR ROMANELLI adjourned the meeting to the Pepperwood Park and Chandler Park tours at
  7:20 p.m. The COMMISSION concurred that no park tour was necessary for Rockbluff Park and
  Silver Spur Park.

  Community Services Director Clark provided an overview of the amenities at each park location
  and the COMMISSIONERS observed and briefly discussed both locations. The only item noted
  for repair was the bender board along the pathway on the west side of the arena at Pepperwoood
  Park.

12.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR ROMANELLI adjourned the meeting at 7:40 p.m. to the next regular Park & Activities
  Commission meeting of Monday, September 17, 2018 beginning at 6:00 p.m. in the Council
  Chamber at Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates,
  CA 90274.
